keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Pohnpei row). The Saudeleur are 'the first organized government uniting the people of Pohnpei island'; the Pohnpei page gives the island's area as 334 km2 (two cells at the grid, about 506 km2). Kosrae, Pingelap and Mokil are not in the polity on the page; the Nahnmwarki period (c. 1628 to c. 1885) is a decentralised system of 'five tribes' / chiefdoms (Pohnpei page; not named) on the same island.

ledger.note: c. 1100: the Saudeleur dynasty unites Pohnpei from Nan Madol. The page: the dynasty ruled 'from c. 1100-1200 CE to c. 1628 CE', 'is thought to have emerged in the 12th century, though exact dates remain uncertain', and was 'the first organized government uniting the people of Pohnpei island'; the Pohnpei page's period table gives c. 1100 to c. 1628. The year is the first of the page's range.

c. 1628: Isokelekel overthrows the Saudeleurs and the Nahnmwarki era begins. Infobox 'conquest by Isokelekel, c. 1628' ('Legend generally dates their downfall to the 1500s' while 'archaeologists date Saudeleur ruins to ca. 1628'); Isokelekel replaced Saudeleur rule with 'the more decentralized nahnmwarki system'. Same island, a new ruling order: a rename, not a new state.

ledger.note: 1886: Spain founds Santiago de la Ascensión at Kolonia. 'By 1886' Spain claimed the Carolines (the period table of the page ends the Nahnmwarki period at c. 1885); the page does not say that Pohnpeian chiefs lost their authority in that year.

certainty.note: A single island: the coast is the border. The dates are soft: both the Saudeleur's start (twelfth century) and fall (the 1500s by legend, c. 1628 by archaeology) are uncertain.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks; drawn as a chiefdom (one dossier for the Saudeleur dynasty and the Nahnmwarki era, joined by a rename at c. 1628 under master-plan rule 2; the five Nahnmwarki chiefdoms are not separated because no page opened names them or gives their lands: Nett, Madolenihmw, U, Kitti and Sokehs appear only as modern municipalities). The date of the Saudeleur's start is a range ('c. 1100-1200', the 12th century) and the fall is c. 1628 against 'the 1500s' in legend; Nan Madol's megalithic construction began around 1180-1200. The page gives the Saudeleur era as 'around 500 years', which does not fit 1100-1628 (the page itself notes this). Not on any page opened: the Spanish-Pohnpeian conflicts of 1887 onward (the Pohnpei page is silent on the 1887 rebellion), the 1899 purchase's effect (German Empire), the Sokehs rebellion's dates. The end 1886 is the Spanish colonial foundation 'by 1886'; real Spanish authority is not documented on these pages. No ruler list: the Saudeleur are listed with '?' dates except Olosohpa (c. 1100-1200) and Saudemwohl (c. 1628), and the page says the count is 'eight to seventeen'. Pohnpei island: Natural Earth admin-1 'Pohnpei' resolves to two cells.
